question: How is Raymond James positioning itself to recruit advisors away from the wirehouses?

claims.text: Trade press (published 2026-11-04, indicative rather than authoritative) reports that an Ohio team moving to Raymond James cited culture and leadership stability, quoting a team member: "Raymond James stands out for its reputation and longstanding stability." The same article says the hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026, as UBS advisors respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.

On the call for the quarter ended 2026-03-31 (published 2026-04-22), CEO Paul Shoukry said the value proposition is "becoming increasingly differentiated": advisers "do not have to choose between culture and capabilities." He described an adviser- and client-focused culture combined with leading technologies, products and solutions. He said this, together with a strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence, "continues to set Raymond James apart for advisers evaluating alternatives." He also pointed to a robust recruiting pipeline, a strong number of advisers committed to join in coming quarters, and more than $1.1 billion in annual technology spend.

On the same call (published 2026-04-22), Shoukry said newer advisers sometimes appreciate Raymond James's technology even more because they come from firms where they saw the alternatives. He said they can be "even more blown away" than advisers who have been at the firm for 25 to 30 years.

On the call for the quarter ended 2025-12-31 (published 2026-01-28), Shoukry described recruiting as "a marathon, not a sprint." He criticised other firms that dial recruiting spending up or down quarter by quarter, saying that approach attracts advisors "moving or not moving for the highest check, and that's not who we're targeting." He said Raymond James has "to have a competitive check" but wants advisors who want to be there long term.

On the same call (published 2026-01-28), Shoukry said the firm broke out retention and transition assistance expense for the first time because, in the last 12 months, it recruited advisors who had $460 million at their prior firms. He said the firm prefers recruiting one by one for cultural fit, and that 100% of transition assistance goes to retention rather than to a seller.

On the call for the quarter ended 2025-09-30 (published 2025-10-22), management reported a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year. Shoukry said that in fiscal 2025 the firm recruited production advisors with prior production of over $400 million, up 21% over last year's record, broad-based across the employee, independent contractor and RCS channels. He called the fiscal 2026 pipeline "probably the strongest it's ever been entering the fiscal year." He described a "best-of-both-worlds value proposition" and said the strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are "proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives."

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) states that the firm's ability to attract high-quality advisors rests on its values-based culture, its commitment to service and the unique ways it serves advisors. It lists the Wealth Management Associate and Advisor Mastery programs, business coaching and growth tools, and separate national conferences for the employee and independent contractor channels.

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) describes multiple affiliation options under the AdvisorChoice® name. Advisors affiliate as employees, as independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through RIA and Custody Services.

The Raymond James recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) presents AdvisorChoice® as five options: Traditional Employee ("book ownership"), Advisor Select (lead your own branch), Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA. It says all are backed by "a leading independent financial firm."

The Traditional Employee page (page content as of 2026-05-16) pitches book ownership, "no quotas, no product pushing," purpose-made technology and a powerful investment platform. The Advisor Select page (page content as of 2026-03-11) offers employee-channel benefits with the independence to build one's own branch and "earn a higher rate on production." The Independent Advisor page (page content as of 2026-05-19) pitches access to a self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer with private wealth, technology and marketing support.

On the call for the quarter ended 2025-06-30 (published 2025-07-23), Shoukry said the recruiting pipeline was growing significantly across all affiliation options. He said the firm had not seen this level of activity "since the financial crisis," and that the advisors now in conversation are much larger than those who came after the crisis. He said the firm is focused on a seamless transition for advisors who affiliate.

On the call for the quarter ended 2025-03-31 (published 2025-04-23), Shoukry said the strong balance sheet becomes increasingly important to prospective advisors seeking strength and stability in periods of stress. He also cited investments such as a new Chief AI Officer role and an in-house AI search tool.

The 2025 10-K (Item 1A, published 2025-11-25) names recruiting-related risks. Competitors frequently claim unfair hiring practices, and the firm has been subject to such claims and may face material litigation. The firm participates, with limited exceptions, in the voluntary Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs client information advisors may take, and some competitors may withdraw from it.

gaps.what: Raymond James's own materials in the evidence do not name the wirehouses as a target or break out recruits by prior firm. Only the trade-press item mentions UBS, and the firm's statements refer generally to "advisors evaluating alternatives."
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James investor-day or earnings materials on recruited advisors' prior-firm mix, or a recruiting-league-table report

gaps.what: Raymond James: Headline payout ranges are published (company recruiting page, as of 2026-04-21); the full payout grid is not public. The page shows Corporate RIA at 81% to 90%. The evidence gives no payout figures or transition-package terms for employee or independent advisors.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James recruiting pages or industry compensation surveys
